This figure is a bar chart showing the accuracy of language models under different conditions. The x-axis represents the language sampling rate, and the y-axis represents the accuracy. The chart includes three series: Low res., High res., and All. The High res. series is the highest, followed by All, and then Low res. The High res. series peaks at around 75% accuracy at a language sampling rate of 0.3, while the Low res. series peaks at around 55% accuracy at the same rate. The All series shows a steady increase in accuracy with higher language sampling rates.

Description: The bar chart compares the accuracy of XLM-7 trained on Wikipedia and CommonCrawl for three language categories: low-resource, high-resource, and all languages. The highest accuracy is achieved by CommonCrawl for low-resource languages, with an approximate difference of 10 points over Wikipedia. For high-resource languages, both Wikipedia and CommonCrawl perform similarly, with a slight advantage for CommonCrawl. For all languages, CommonCrawl again shows a higher accuracy, approximately 5 points above Wikipedia.

This bar chart compares the accuracy of models with fixed and increased capacity across three different numbers of languages: 7, 30, and 100. The blue bars represent models with fixed capacity, while the orange bars represent models with increased capacity. The highest accuracy is observed in the fixed capacity model with 7 languages, reaching approximately 72. The lowest accuracy is seen in the fixed capacity model with 100 languages, around 67. The increased capacity models show higher accuracy across all language counts, with the highest being around 72 for 30 languages.
